card.title: Nintendo Switch Charging, Power, and Video Diagnostics Procedure

claims.statement: The USB charger fuse can be tested for continuity with a multimeter to check if power passes from the USB-C port to the battery chip.
claims.evidence: Testing both sides of the fuse in continuity mode reveals if it is blown.
claims.quote: Lets check the fuse that lets power from USB C reach the battery chip. Unplug the battery. With a multimeter set to continuity mode, put one probe in one side of the fuse and the other probe in the other side of the fuse

claims.statement: If the replacement USB charger fuse is needed, an equivalent rating like 0.315a or higher is recommended.
claims.evidence: The original R type Matsuo fuse is rated 0.315a which is stated to be too low.
claims.quote: About this fuse.. Looks like an R type - It could be a Matsuo fuse. Their R rated are 0.315a. Which is FAR too low. If you need to replace – I would go for this one or equivalent: https://ro.mouser.com/ProductDetail/Litt

claims.statement: Battery charging functionality can be verified by measuring the voltage across battery connector cables before and after charging for 30 minutes.
claims.evidence: Measuring voltage increase on the red battery cables confirms the console is charging and the BQ24193 is functioning.
claims.quote: After that plug the battery back in and, without touching the power button, put the switch charging for 30 minutes. After the 30 minutes, unplug it of the charger, redo everything that I said. If the voltage after 30 min

claims.statement: Shorts to ground on capacitors or around the M92T36 chip indicate faults that require component removal to isolate.
claims.evidence: Continuity on both sides of a capacitor when probed against ground indicates a short.
claims.quote: With a multimeter set to continuity mode, put the black probe on a good ground... and with the red probe check every capacitor... continuity in both sides of the capacitor means short to ground.

claims.statement: Pin 5 and Pin 6 of the M92T36 chip should read between 3v to 6v when the console is powered on with the battery connected.
claims.evidence: Voltage measurements taken with DC voltage mode on M92T36 pins or their corresponding trace capacitors.
claims.quote: In that pin you are supposed to have 3v to 6v. If you have 0v or less, you have a short on that line... its suppose to have between 3v to 6v. 0v in pin 6 means M92T36 is bad.

claims.statement: If a Switch running firmware version 7.x.x shows no display, leaving it charging all night and entering recovery mode for 2 hours or more is suggested.
claims.evidence: Procedure workaround for firmware 7.x.x display issues.
claims.quote: If you know that your console is in version 7.x.x, sorry but for now the only thing that you can do is leave it charging all night and trying to put it to recovery mode and leave it there for 2 hours or more.

claims.statement: Entering RCM mode and injecting the hekate payload determines if a blank screen is caused by firmware issues rather than hardware failure.
claims.evidence: If the screen turns on with hekate payload, the console hardware and firmware are mismatched or corrupt.
claims.quote: If the screen turns right on with hekate payload, your console is fine, the firmware is not... If even the payload method failed, you probably will have a PI3USB30532 bad or the CPU is just dead af.

claims.statement: The PI3USB30532 chip manages routing of USB 3.0 and DisplayPort 1.2 signals through the USB Type-C connector.
claims.evidence: Functional description of PI3USB30532 chip applications.
claims.quote: So, with the board upside down you'll see just above the USB C connector is a rectangular chip - this is PI3USB30532, a "6:4 differential channel bi-directional matrix switch solution for switching USB3.0 and/or DP1.2 si

procedure: Unplug the battery and set the multimeter to continuity mode to test both sides of the USB charger fuse.
Measure the voltage on the red battery connector wires with a DC voltmeter, charge the console for 30 minutes, and re-measure to verify if the BQ24193 charges the battery.
Check capacitors across the front and back of the motherboard for shorts to ground using continuity mode with the black probe on ground.
Test M92T36 pin 5 and pin 6 (or their connected trace capacitors) for 3v to 6v DC with the battery connected and power button clicked.
Inspect screen and backlight ribbon cables and connectors visually.
Attempt to boot into RCM mode and inject the hekate payload if the screen remains black and firmware is below 7.x.x.
cautions: SOURCE RISK: Using third-party docks can cause charging ports to fail or brick consoles.
card.caveats: Always verify firmware version constraints before attempting software recovery workarounds.
